title: claude t4
prompt: Create ledgerkit/slots.py with free_slots(busy, day_start, day_end, min_minutes=0). busy is a list of (start, end) timezone-aware datetimes, possibly overlapping, unsorted, and in different UTC offsets. day_start and day_end are timezone-aware datetimes. Return the free gaps inside [day_start, day_end] as a sorted list of (start, end) tuples, expressed in the timezone of day_start. Busy intervals are clipped to the window; ones entirely outside are ignored; touching busy intervals merge, so no zero-length gap is returned. Only keep gaps at least min_minutes long. Raise ValueError if any datetime is naive, if any interval has end < start, or if day_end <= day_start. Zero-length busy intervals are ignored. Add tests in tests/test_slots.py and run python3 -m pytest -q.
summary:
I added `free_slots` in `ledgerkit/slots.py` with tests in `tests/test_slots.py`, and committed both on `crew/1107-10d03b` as 33c6266. `python3 -m pytest -q` gives 12 passed, which covers the 11 new slot tests and the existing money test file. I haven't pushed anything.

The tests cover these cases:
- unsorted and overlapping busy intervals
- touching intervals, which leave no zero-length gap
- clipping to the window, and intervals entirely outside it
- the `min_minutes` filter
- zero-length busy intervals
- mixed UTC offsets, with output in `day_start`'s timezone
- every `ValueError` case

One behaviour to be aware of: busy intervals are validated even when they fall outside the window. A naive datetime or an interval with `end < start` raises `ValueError` regardless of where it sits.
